children: Every enterprise seller has had the same quarter. The meetings go well. The buyer is engaged. The forecast holds. And the deal still takes nine months to close, because the work that moves it forward keeps landing in the gaps between conversations.
We looked at five enterprise instances of AgentPress over six months and tracked where the calendar actually went. The meetings were not the problem.
The median deal spent 71% of its life waiting
on something a human had to sit down and produce.

The waiting is rarely dramatic. It is a follow-up that goes out four days late, a security questionnaire that sits with the wrong person, a business case that only gets built once the buyer asks twice.
Broken down across the deals we reviewed, the recurring gaps were consistent:
Prep for a discovery call written the morning of, or not at all
Post-call recaps sent late enough that the buyer had already moved on
Stakeholder maps that lived in one rep's head and left with them
Business cases assembled by the champion, at night, without the numbers
None of these lose a deal on their own. Together they add months.

The most expensive gap is the one you never see. Your champion walks into a finance review you are not invited to, carrying a value story they built themselves from a pricing page and a slide. They are defending your product with your worst available evidence.
CRM hygiene does not win deals. Understanding the buyer, the value, and what needs to happen next does.
The fix was not more reminders. It was moving the work off the rep's queue entirely, so that the artifact exists before anyone asks for it. In practice that meant a specific sequence:
Reconstruct the account from email, transcripts, and CRM the moment the opportunity is created
Produce the prep brief and discovery questions the day before every call, unprompted
Capture commitments, objections, and stakeholders from the transcript within minutes of hangup
Build the value model from the buyer's own operating numbers, then keep it current
Publish it all to a deal room the champion can forward without editing
The order matters. A business case built before you understand the buyer is a template, and buyers can tell.
Across the same five instances, cycle time fell by a median of 38 days. The change was not that reps worked faster. It was that the deal stopped waiting on them.
The artifacts arrived before the buyer thought to ask.

children: to build full-stack product, AI agent orchestration systems, embeddable widgets, and enterprise integrations.
This is a hands-on building role, not a ticket-closing role. You'll work directly with the VP of Engineering across the full stack.
This is a full-time W-2 role and can be done remotely from the US or Canada, with 4-6 weekday hours overlapping US time zones.
You will own features end to end, from the data layer through the interface a client actually touches:
Build and ship end-to-end features across Bun/Hono/Elysia backends, React/Next.js frontends, and typically PostgreSQL data layers.
Work within our AI agent orchestration system: tool execution pipelines, RAG retrieval, multi-agent coordination, and real-time streaming via WebSockets.
Develop and maintain embeddable IIFE chat widgets deployed across client environments with complex CSP and integration constraints.
Interface directly with enterprise clients on technical integrations, troubleshoot production issues, and communicate clearly without hand-holding.
Contribute to infrastructure: CI/CD pipelines, background job processing with BullMQ, caching layers with Redis, and monitoring.
Write code that other people can read. Participate in code reviews and hold yourself to a high bar.

This is a TypeScript-first codebase, and the stack is what you'll be in every day. You don't need to have shipped all of it, but you should be able to read an existing codebase, understand why it was built that way, and extend it without breaking conventions.
We're looking for a developer who can think independently, move fast, and write clean code without constant direction. Concretely, that means:
Strong TypeScript proficiency across both frontend and backend. This is a TypeScript-first codebase.
Solid experience with React and at least one Node.js-based server framework. Familiarity with Bun, Hono, or Next.js is a strong plus.
Comfort working with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, and understanding query performance.
Ability to read an existing codebase, understand architectural decisions, and extend them without breaking conventions.
Ability to clearly articulate technical direction and back it up. You should be comfortable defending your own ideas and challenging others. We welcome discourse.
Excellent written and verbal English communication. You will interact with enterprise clients and need to be clear, professional, and confident in technical conversations.
Self-directed work ethic. You know when to push through ambiguity on your own and when to flag something early. You do not wait to be told what to do.
Experience with or genuine interest in AI/LLM tooling, prompt engineering, RAG systems, or agent architectures.
Prior work where you owned features end to end, preferably in a startup or small-team environment.
Willing to overlap by 4-6 hours during weekdays with US time zones for real-time collaboration.
Based in the US or Canada. This is a remote role, but we can only hire candidates authorized to work in the US or Canada.
None of these are required, but they'll shorten your ramp:
Experience building embeddable widgets or third-party integrations with complex browser constraints such as CSP, CORS, and iframe sandboxing.
Familiarity with real-time systems: WebSockets, streaming APIs, or event-driven architectures.
Background in SaaS products, especially B2B or developer tools.
Experience with Clerk, Stripe, or similar third-party auth/payment integrations.
We want to be upfront so nobody wastes their time:
If you need detailed specs and wireframes before you can start building, this is not the right fit. We move fast and expect you to fill in gaps.
If you write code that works but nobody else can maintain, we will have problems. Readability matters as much as functionality here.
If you disappear when you hit a blocker instead of communicating, this will not work. We are remote-first and trust is built through transparency.
If you are looking for a job where you coast and collect a paycheck, look elsewhere. We are building something real and need people who give a damn.
This is a full-time W-2 role with equity.
If you come in, ship consistently, and prove you can own a domain, there is a clear path to a senior engineering role with significantly higher compensation. We promote based on output, not tenure.

children: Before AgentPress, we were a services firm. We built bespoke AI agents for B2B SaaS revenue teams, but we were a body shop. We built what clients asked for, collected the check, and moved on.
Then something happened that I couldn't ignore.

I was at the company kickoff for one of our customers, HiveMQ — an enterprise SaaS business. Their executive leadership team was demoing the suite of agents we'd built for them. One by one they walked through the tools: onboarding agent, support agent, SDR agent. Polite applause. Good stuff.
Then they showed the last one — our business value assessment agent. It generates a fully quantified business case for any prospect in seconds. Custom to the account. Backed by real financial data.
150 people gave it a spontaneous standing ovation. I'd never seen anything like it at a corporate event.

children: After the event, investors and partners who had been in the room started contacting me. They didn't care about the other agents. They wanted to talk about value selling.
The wedge isn't agents. The wedge is value.
What we learned the hard way

We launched AgentPress on Labor Day 2025. Initially, we thought we were building a generalist platform for customer-facing AI agents — an SDR for your marketing website, an onboarding planner, a support agent, a renewals assistant. A unified suite.
The technology was strong, but the positioning was weak. Every AI startup and their dog was building customer-facing agents. A "unified suite" wasn't enough to differentiate us.
B2B revenue is fundamentally broken because every touchpoint tells a different value story.
The marketing site says one thing. The AE pitches another. The business case says something else. Post-sales, nobody's tracking whether the promised value was actually delivered.

When your value story is fragmented, you get customers with unrealistic expectations, unmet promises, higher churn, and lower renewals. It doesn't matter how good your agents are if they're each telling a different story.
The real breakthrough was making every agent in the suite value-aware — powered by a unified, patented value model that ensures a consistent, quantifiable value story at every customer touchpoint.

Nobody else is doing this. Incumbents are siloed — they build point solutions for support, or SDR, or sales enablement. They don't own the value story across the lifecycle. They can't, because they don't have the underlying model.
Since launching AgentPress in September, we've been averaging 27% month-over-month ARR growth. We hit $576K ARR in six months, with $2.3M in pipeline and five live enterprise instances.

When you give a revenue team the ability to sell on quantifiable value at every touchpoint, they don't want to go back.
Here's something I believe about B2B sales that most people haven't caught onto yet:
AI agents are going to control purchasing decisions.

Not in some distant future. Soon. And when AI is on the other side of the table evaluating your product, it will be ruthless. It won't be swayed by a charming AE or a nice slide deck. It will demand quantifiable business justification, backed by real data, specific to the buyer's situation.

The companies that can generate that justification instantly — at every touchpoint, for every prospect, with every agent — will win. The ones that can't will lose deals they never even knew they were in.

That's what AgentPress is building: the value-aware agentic operating system for revenue teams. A platform where every customer-facing agent — and eventually every internal agent — speaks the language of quantifiable value.
